mainTopic: The partition in the second בית המקדש, plaster in wall measurements, רב חסדא's rule against tearing down a בית כנסת, and the story of הורדוס
overview: The amud opens by closing an argument: the second בית המקדש was greater than the first both in height and in years. That leads to a question about why its partition was made only of curtains. The answer is that a very tall wall cannot stand without a ceiling, and אביי has a tradition that the partition must be all wall or all curtain. Next the גמרא asks whether the משנה's wall thicknesses include the plaster. Several proofs are brought, and each one is pushed off. Then רב חסדא rules that one may not tear down a בית כנסת before building a new one, and the גמרא discusses the reasons for the rule, its limits, and an exception for a cracked building. This raises the question of how בבא בן בוטא could advise הורדוס to tear down the בית המקדש. That leads into the story of how הורדוס, a former slave, seized the throne and killed the רבנן, sparing only בבא בן בוטא. The story continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The second Temple was greater in both height and years
steps.stepSummary: The earlier argument ended with one view saying the second בית המקדש was greater 'in years.' The גמרא now says both views are true.
steps.simpleTranslation: The other view said the second Temple was greater in years. And in fact this is true and that is true.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the earlier argument over how the second בית המקדש was 'greater' than the first. It concludes that both answers are correct.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One view said 'greater' means taller. The other said it means it lasted longer. The גמרא says there is no real argument: the second בית המקדש was both taller and longer-lasting.

keyTerms.meaning: In years, meaning it lasted longer
This is true and that is true; both are correct

steps.whyThisMatters: Once we accept that the second בית המקדש really was much taller, the next questions follow: how could a partition reach that height?

phrases.english: In years.
phrases.notes: This is the end of the earlier argument over the פסוק saying the last House would be greater. One view said it was greater in years.

phrases.english: And this is so, and that is so.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the argument from the end of the previous section of the daf
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The second בית המקדש was greater than the first both in height and in how long it stood.

steps.title: Why not build a thirty-cubit wall and add a curtain above?
steps.stepSummary: If the second בית המקדש was taller, they could have built a wall thirty אמות high, like in the first בית המקדש, and finished the rest with a curtain.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let them build thirty cubits as a wall, and make the rest a curtain!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the way the second בית המקדש was set up. It asks why they did not use a wall for part of the height and a curtain for the rest.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the second בית המקדש the partition was made only of curtains. The challenge says a wall of thirty אמות had already worked in the first בית המקדש, so they could have kept that and covered only the extra height with a curtain.

keyTerms.meaning: A built structure, here a stone wall
A curtain, here the curtain separating the קודש הקדשים

phrases.english: But let them make thirty cubits as a built wall,
and make the rest a curtain!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the conclusion that the second בית המקדש was taller
steps.kashyaTarget: The practice of using only curtains in the second בית המקדש
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A thirty-cubit wall already worked in the first בית המקדש, so they could have combined a wall below with a curtain above.

steps.title: A thirty-cubit wall only stood thanks to the ceiling
steps.stepSummary: The thirty-cubit wall in the first בית המקדש stood only because the ceiling and the plaster layer above held it. On its own it would not stand.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even when a thirty-cubit wall stood, it stood because of the ceiling and plaster. Without the ceiling and plaster, it would not have stood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that a thirty-cubit wall cannot stand by itself. It needs a ceiling holding it in place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first בית המקדש, the ceiling sat at thirty אמות and held the top of the wall firm. In the taller second בית המקדש, the ceiling was much higher, so a thirty-cubit wall would have had nothing holding its top and would have fallen.

keyTerms.meaning: A layer of plaster or packed material on the ceiling

phrases.english: Even when thirty cubits stood,
it stood because of the ceiling and the plaster layer;

phrases.aramaic: בְּלֹא תִּקְרָה וּמַעֲזִיבָה – לָא הֲוָה קָאֵי.
phrases.english: without ceiling and plaster, it would not stand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 2
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since a thirty-cubit wall stood in the first בית המקדש, it could stand in the second too.
steps.terutzMaskana: It stood only because the ceiling held it. Without a ceiling at that height, it would fall.

steps.title: Then build as high a wall as possible and add a curtain
steps.stepSummary: Even if thirty אמות could not stand alone, they could have built the wall as high as it could stand and finished the rest with a curtain.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let them build whatever height is possible as a wall, and make the rest a curtain!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes again. It asks why they did not build a shorter wall that could stand by itself and use a curtain above it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous answer only showed that thirty אמות was too tall. It did not rule out a shorter wall. So the question comes back: why not mix a wall and a curtain at all?

phrases.english: But let them make whatever is possible as a wall,
and make the rest a curtain!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges whether the answer in step 3 is enough
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that a thirty-cubit wall could not stand
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A shorter wall that can stand on its own would avoid that problem, so a mixed wall and curtain still seems possible.

steps.title: אביי: the partition must be all wall or all curtain
steps.stepSummary: אביי reports a tradition that the partition must be entirely a wall, as in the first בית המקדש, or entirely a curtain, as in the משכן. A mix is not allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: We have a tradition: either all of it is a wall or all of it is a curtain. All a wall, as in the Temple; all a curtain, as in the Tabernacle.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers that mixing is not an option. By tradition, the partition must be fully one thing or fully the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the reason is no longer physical but a received rule. There are only two models: the first בית המקדש had a full wall, and the משכן had a full curtain. Since there is no model for a mixed partition, the second בית המקדש used only curtains.
steps.whatToRemember: The partition before the קודש הקדשים can be all wall (like the first בית המקדש) or all curtain (like the משכן), never a mix. That is why the second בית המקדש used curtains only.

phrases.english: Abaye said: We have a tradition:

phrases.aramaic: אִי כּוּלְּהוּ בְּבִנְיָן, אִי כּוּלְּהוּ בְּפָרוֹכֶת.
phrases.english: either all of it as a wall, or all of it as a curtain.
Either all as a wall — from the Temple,
or all as a curtain — from the Tabernacle.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 4 and closes this line of questions
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A partition could be partly wall and partly curtain.
steps.terutzMaskana: Tradition allows only a full wall or a full curtain, based on the בית המקדש and the משכן.

steps.title: Do the משנה's wall measurements include the plaster?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the wall thicknesses listed in the משנה include the plaster coating or measure only the building material.
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: Are the measurements the materials together with their plaster, or perhaps the materials without their plaster?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic. It returns to the משנה's list of wall thicknesses and asks whether the plaster is counted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gives a set thickness for walls made of different materials. The question is whether that number already includes the plaster on the wall or refers only to the stones or bricks themselves.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked among them

phrases.english: A question was asked among them:
Are the measurements them with their plaster,
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the wall materials whose thickness the משנה lists, like stones and bricks.

phrases.english: or perhaps them without their plaster?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question about the משנה's measurements
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the משנה's wall thicknesses include the plaster

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק: the measurements include the plaster
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק argues that the measurements must include the plaster. If they did not, the משנה would have had to give a separate measurement for the plaster.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: It makes sense that it means with the plaster. If you think it means without the plaster, the משנה should have taught the plaster's measurement! So isn't it clear: with their plaster?
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק tries to prove an answer from what the משנה does not say. It never mentions a size for the plaster.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His logic: if plaster were added on top of the listed thickness, the full wall would be thicker than stated. The משנה would then need to tell us how much plaster to add. Since it does not, the plaster must already be included in the numbers.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense, it is reasonable
It enters your mind, you might think

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק, מִסְתַּבְּרָא:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said: It makes sense:
them with their plaster;

phrases.aramaic: דְּאִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ הֵן בְּלֹא סִידָן,
phrases.english: for if it entered your mind that it is them without their plaster,
let it teach its measurement!

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לָאו שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ: הֵן וְסִידָן?
phrases.english: Rather, isn't it so — learn from this: them with their plaster?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק, מִסְתַּבְּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a proof to answer the question in step 6
steps.raayaObject: That the measurements include the plaster
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's silence about any separate measurement for plaster

steps.title: The plaster is too thin to mention
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. The measurements may really leave out the plaster, and the משנה skipped it because plaster is less than a טפח thick.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Really, I can tell you it means without their plaster. Since the plaster is not a handbreadth thick, the משנה did not mention it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב נחמן בר יצחק's proof. It gives another reason the משנה might not mention plaster.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof relied on the idea that the משנה would have to mention plaster if it were extra. The גמרא answers that the משנה only lists sizes of at least a טפח. Plaster is thinner than that, so leaving it out proves nothing.
steps.confusionAlert: This does not decide that the plaster is left out. It only shows that רב נחמן בר יצחק's proof does not work, so the question stays open.

phrases.english: No; really I can tell you:
them without their plaster;

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵיוָן דְּלָא הָוֵי טֶפַח, לָא תָּנֵי.
phrases.english: and since it is not a handbreadth, it did not teach it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof in step 7
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof is rejected; the question itself is not decided
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה's silence can be explained by plaster being less than a טפח, so it would not be listed anyway.

steps.title: But the משנה does list half-handbreadths
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the claim that the משנה skips amounts smaller than a טפח. In the case of bricks, the משנה says each neighbor gives a טפח and a half.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the משנה teaches about bricks: this one gives a טפח and a half, and that one gives a טפח and a half!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from Step 8. That answer said the משנה would not bother mentioning plaster because it is less than a טפח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In our משנה, a brick wall is three טפחים thick, and each neighbor gives a טפח and a half. So the משנה clearly does mention a half-טפח. If it is willing to mention small amounts, it should have mentioned the plaster too.

keyTerms.meaning: But doesn't it teach…? (opens a challenge from a source)

phrases.english: But doesn't it teach: with bricks,
this one gives a handbreadth and a half
and that one gives a handbreadth and a half!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the דחיה of Step 8
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the משנה leaves out amounts smaller than a טפח
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה itself lists half-טפח amounts for bricks, so small size is not a reason to skip the plaster.

steps.title: The halves combine into whole handbreadths
steps.stepSummary: The half-טפחים are mentioned only because together they add up to full טפחים.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, the halves are fit to be combined into a whole measure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The two halves are mentioned because they join to make a full amount.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each neighbor's טפח and a half adds up to a complete three-טפח wall, so the half is part of a whole measurement. Plaster is a thin coat that does not add up to a full טפח, so the משנה had no reason to mention it.

phrases.english: There, they are fit to be combined.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 9
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה mentions small amounts, so it should have mentioned the plaster too.
steps.terutzMaskana: Halves are mentioned only when they combine into full טפחים. Thin plaster does not, so the explanation of Step 8 still stands.

steps.title: Proof from the beam over an alleyway
steps.stepSummary: A משנה in עירובין says the beam must hold a half-brick, and a full brick is three טפחים. That brick has no plaster, which suggests our משנה's three-טפח brick wall has no plaster either.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: the beam they spoke of must be wide enough to hold a half-brick, and a half-brick is half of a brick that is three טפחים wide!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new proof that the measurements in our משנה do not include plaster.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In עירובין, a brick is called three טפחים wide, and a brick set on a beam has no plaster. If a plain brick is already three טפחים, then the three-טפח brick wall in our משנה is measured without the plaster.

keyTerms.meaning: a beam placed across an alleyway so one may carry there on שבת

phrases.english: Come and hear:
The beam that they spoke of
phrases.notes: This is the beam from מסכת עירובין, placed over an alleyway so people may carry in it on שבת.

phrases.english: must be wide enough to hold a half-brick,
and the half-brick is half a brick
of three handbreadths!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first proof was set aside, a new proof is brought for the same question
steps.raayaObject: That the wall thicknesses in our משנה do not include plaster
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in עירובין about the beam and the half-brick

steps.title: That case speaks of large bricks
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. The brick in עירובין is a large brick that is a full three טפחים by itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, it is talking about large bricks.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes off the proof from עירובין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bricks come in different sizes. The עירובין brick is a large one, three טפחים without plaster. Our משנה may mean smaller bricks that reach three טפחים only with the plaster.

phrases.english: There, it is talking about large ones.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the ראיה of Step 11
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof only; the question of plaster stays open
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed all bricks are the same size, but עירובין speaks of large bricks.

steps.title: The wording in עירובין supports the large-brick answer
steps.stepSummary: The עירובין משנה says a brick 'of three טפחים,' which suggests there are also smaller bricks.
steps.simpleTranslation: The wording is precise too, since it says 'of three טפחים.' This implies there is also a small brick. Learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up the answer from Step 12 by looking closely at the words of the עירובין משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If every brick were three טפחים, the משנה would only need to say 'half a brick.' Adding 'of three טפחים' shows it means one specific size, so smaller bricks must exist. The גמרא accepts this with 'learn from it.'

keyTerms.meaning: the wording is precise too (supports the answer)
learn from it (the point is accepted)

steps.whatToRemember: The question of whether the wall measurements include plaster is never proven either way here. Each proof is pushed off.

phrases.english: The wording is precise too, since it teaches:
"of three handbreadths,"
which implies there is a small one;
learn from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the דחיה of Step 12 from the wording of the source
steps.raayaObject: That the עירובין משנה speaks of large bricks
steps.raayaSupportSource: The extra words 'of three טפחים' in the עירובין משנה

steps.title: Do not tear down a synagogue before building a new one
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא rules that a person may not tear down a בית כנסת until he has built another one.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: A person should not tear down a בית כנסת until he builds another בית כנסת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new topic with a ruling from רב חסדא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a new הלכה. Even if someone plans to rebuild a בית כנסת, he must first build the new one, and only then take down the old one.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a practical rule about rebuilding or replacing a בית כנסת.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
A person should not tear down a synagogue
until he builds another synagogue.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, unconnected to the plaster discussion
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A בית כנסת may not be torn down until a replacement has been built.

steps.title: Two reasons for רב חסדא's rule
steps.stepSummary: Some say the reason is that he might fail to rebuild. Others say it is so people are not left without a place to pray.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say it is because of negligence, and some say it is because of prayer.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives two different explanations for why רב חסדא made his rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first reason worries that once the old building is down, the person may never get around to building the new one. The second reason worries that while the new building goes up, there is nowhere to daven. The two reasons may lead to different results in certain cases.

phrases.english: There are those who say: because of negligence,
phrases.notes: He means the worry is that once it's torn down, the new one might never get built.

phrases.english: and there are those who say: because of prayer.
phrases.notes: Meanwhile, people would have nowhere to daven.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason behind רב חסדא's ruling in Step 14
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There are two reasons for the rule: fear of negligence, or the loss of a place to pray.

steps.title: What is the difference between the two reasons?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical difference there is between the two reasons given for רב חסדא's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks when the two reasons from the last step would lead to different results. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One reason was the fear that the new building might never get built. The other was that people should not be left without a place to pray. The גמרא wants a case where only one of these reasons applies.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference between them? It asks for a case where two views give different results.

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the practical difference between the two reasons listed in step 15.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A case where the two reasons give different rulings.

steps.title: The difference: a town that has another בית כנסת
steps.stepSummary: The two reasons differ when the town has another בית כנסת to pray in.
steps.simpleTranslation: The difference between them is a case where there is another בית כנסת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two reasons differ when the town already has a second בית כנסת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If there is another בית כנסת, people still have a place to pray, so the second reason does not apply. The first reason still applies, because the new building might never be built. So under the first reason it is still forbidden, and under the second it is allowed.

phrases.english: There is a difference between them
where there is another synagogue.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: When another בית כנסת exists, only the 'it might not get rebuilt' reason still forbids tearing down first.

steps.title: מרימר and מר זוטרא built in the off-season
steps.stepSummary: מרימר and מר זוטרא rebuilt a summer בית כנסת during the winter and a winter one during the summer.
steps.simpleTranslation: מרימר and מר זוטרא would tear down and build the summer בית כנסת in winter, and build the winter one in summer.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells how two אמוראים rebuilt their buildings while keeping to רב חסדא's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: They had two buildings, one used in summer and one used in winter. Each was rebuilt during the season when it was not in use, so the town always had a place to pray.

phrases.english: Mareimar and Mar Zutra
would tear down and build the summer synagogue in the winter,
and build the winter synagogue in the summer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows how רב חסדא's rule was carried out in practice.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Rebuild a seasonal בית כנסת during the season it is not used, so there is always a place to pray.

steps.title: What if the money is already collected?
steps.stepSummary: רבינא asks רב אשי whether one may tear down first if the money for the new building has already been collected.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to רב אשי: If the money has been collected and is set aside, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא asks about a case where the money for the new building is already collected and waiting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the worry is that the new building will never get built, ready money might seem to remove that worry. רבינא asks whether this is enough to allow tearing down first.

keyTerms.meaning: They are set aside, lying ready

phrases.english: Ravina said to Rav Ashi:
If the money was collected and set aside, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question about the limits of רב חסדא's rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether collected money removes the worry and allows tearing down first.

steps.title: No, the money might go to redeem captives
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that the money might be given to redeem captives, so it is still forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Perhaps a need to redeem captives will come up, and they will give the money for that.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי says that ready money is not enough, because it could be used for something more urgent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Redeeming captives is a very urgent מצוה, and money set aside for a בית כנסת may be used for it. Then the town would be left with no building at all, so the worry remains.

phrases.english: He said to him: Perhaps there will come up for them
a need to redeem captives, and they will give it to them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: דִּילְמָא מִיתְרְמֵי לְהוּ פִּדְיוֹן שְׁבוּיִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבינא's question in step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Still forbidden, since the money might be used for פדיון שבויים.

steps.title: What if the building materials are ready?
steps.stepSummary: רבינא asks about a case where the bricks, boards, and beams are already prepared.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the bricks are piled up, the boards are prepared, and the beams are set out, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא goes a step further and asks about a case where the actual building materials are ready, not just money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Materials seem less likely to be used for something else than cash. So maybe here one may tear down first.

keyTerms.meaning: The bricks are piled in rows

phrases.english: If the bricks are piled up and the boards are prepared,
and the beams are set out, what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁרִיגִי לִיבְנֵי, וְהָדְרִי הוּדְרֵי, וּמַחֲתִי כְּשׁוּרֵי, מַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 20 by asking about a stronger case: materials instead of money.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether ready building materials allow tearing down first.

steps.title: No, they might sell the materials for captives
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that the materials might be sold to pay for redeeming captives.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Sometimes a need to redeem captives comes up, and they sell the materials and give the money for it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי says the same worry applies, because materials can be sold.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Materials are not safer than money, because they can be sold for cash. So it is still forbidden to tear down first.

phrases.english: He said to him: Sometimes there comes up for them
a need to redeem captives, and they sell the materials and give the money for it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: זִמְנִין דְּמִתְרְמֵי לְהוּ פִּדְיוֹן שְׁבוּיִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Still forbidden, since the materials might be sold for פדיון שבויים.

steps.title: Then even a finished building could be sold!
steps.stepSummary: רבינא objects: if materials might be sold, then even a finished building might be sold.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, even when they have built it, the same worry should apply!
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא challenges רב אשי's reasoning by pushing it to the extreme.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If we worry that materials will be sold for captives, we could worry the same about a finished new building. Then one could never replace an old בית כנסת at all.

keyTerms.meaning: If so, a phrase that opens a challenge

phrases.english: If so, even if they built it, the same should apply!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reasoning of step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's worry that things set aside for the building could be sold for captives.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same worry should apply to a finished building, which would make rebuilding impossible.

steps.title: People do not sell a finished building
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that people do not sell a building they live in or use.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: People do not sell their dwellings.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי explains why a finished building is different from loose materials.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Money and materials are easy to give away. A building that people use is not sold, even for urgent needs. So once the new building stands, the worry is gone.

keyTerms.meaning: His dwelling, a building in use

steps.whatToRemember: One may not tear down an old בית כנסת first, even if money or materials are ready, because they might go to פדיון שבויים. A finished building is safe, because people do not sell buildings they use.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: דִּירְתֵיהּ דְּאִינָשֵׁי לָא מְזַבְּנִי.
phrases.english: He said to him: People do not sell their dwellings.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: דִּירְתֵיהּ דְּאִינָשֵׁי לָא מְזַבְּנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction between movable materials and a building in use
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A finished building could also be sold for captives.
steps.terutzMaskana: People do not sell a building they use, so only money and materials are at risk.

steps.title: Exception: a cracked building may be torn down first
steps.stepSummary: The rule applies only when the old בית כנסת has no cracks. If it is cracked, one may tear it down first and then build.
steps.simpleTranslation: We said this only when no cracks are seen in it. But if cracks are seen, they tear it down and then build.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא limits רב חסדא's rule: it applies only to a sound building.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A cracked building is dangerous and cannot really be used to pray in safely. So the rule against tearing down first does not apply, and one may tear down right away.

keyTerms.meaning: We said this only when, a phrase that limits a rule

phrases.english: And we said this only
where no cracks are seen in it,
but if cracks are seen in it,
they tear it down and then build.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא דְּלָא חָזֵי בָּהּ תִּיוְהָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to רב חסדא's main rule and limits it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the old בית כנסת has cracks, one may tear it down before building the new one.

steps.title: רב אשי tore down the cracked בית כנסת in מתא מחסיא
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי saw cracks in the בית כנסת of מתא מחסיא, tore it down, and moved his bed there until the new building was finished, down to the drainpipes.
steps.simpleTranslation: Like the case of רב אשי, who saw cracks in the בית כנסת of מתא מחסיא. He tore it down, brought his bed there, and did not take it out until they had put up the drainpipes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא supports the exception with a story about רב אשי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי tore down the cracked building first, as the exception allows. He also slept at the site to make sure the work kept going and finished quickly. This shows that the worry about the building being left unfinished was still taken seriously.

keyTerms.meaning: The town of רב אשי, home of his ישיבה
Drainpipes, the final touches of the building

steps.whyThisMatters: The story shows that even when tearing down first is allowed, one should make sure the new בית כנסת gets finished.

phrases.english: Like this case of Rav Ashi,
who saw cracks in it,
in the synagogue of Mata Meḥasya.
He tore it down and brought his bed in there,
and he did not take it out
until they had fixed drainpipes to it.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי הָא דְּרַב אָשֵׁי חֲזָא בָּהּ תִּיוְהָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a real case that supports the exception in step 25.
steps.raayaObject: The ruling that a cracked בית כנסת may be torn down before rebuilding.
steps.raayaSupportSource: What רב אשי did with the בית כנסת of מתא מחסיא.

steps.title: How could בבא בן בוטא tell הורדוס to tear down the בית המקדש?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges בבא בן בוטא's advice to הורדוס from רב חסדא's rule against tearing down a בית כנסת before a new one is built.
steps.simpleTranslation: How could בבא בן בוטא advise הורדוס to tear down the בית המקדש? Didn't רב חסדא say that a person may not tear down a בית כנסת until he builds another one?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings up a story where בבא בן בוטא told הורדוס to tear down the בית המקדש and rebuild it. It asks how that is allowed, given רב חסדא's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא's rule says you must build the new building first, so the community is never left without one. If that is true for a simple בית כנסת, it should be even more true for the בית המקדש. So בבא בן בוטא's advice seems to go against the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: A great sage who lived in the time of הורדוס

phrases.aramaic: וּבָבָא בֶּן בּוּטָא, הֵיכִי אַסְּבֵיהּ לֵיהּ עֵצָה
phrases.english: And Bava ben Buta, how could he give advice
to Herod to tear down the Temple?
But didn't Rav Chisda say:
A person should not tear down a shul
until he builds another shul!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבָבָא בֶּן בּוּטָא, הֵיכִי אַסְּבֵיהּ לֵיהּ עֵצָה לְהוֹרְדוֹס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies רב חסדא's rule to a historical case and finds an apparent contradiction.
steps.kashyaTarget: בבא בן בוטא's advice to tear down the בית המקדש
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב חסדא forbids tearing down a בית כנסת before building a new one, so tearing down the בית המקדש first should be forbidden too.

steps.title: First answer: the Temple had cracks
steps.stepSummary: The building was cracked, so it was allowed to tear it down first.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say that he saw cracks in it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a first answer: the בית המקדש building had cracks.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already learned that if the old building is cracked, you may tear it down before building. So בבא בן בוטא's advice fits that exception and does not break רב חסדא's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: If you want, say (introduces one possible answer)

phrases.english: If you want, say:
he saw cracks in it,

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי בָּעֵית אֵימָא: תִּיוְהָא חֲזָא בֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא by applying the cracks exception.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Places the case under a known exception
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The בית המקדש was a sound building, so tearing it down first was forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: The building was cracked, so tearing it down first was allowed.

steps.title: Second answer: a king does not back down
steps.stepSummary: A government is different, because it does not go back on its plans.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or if you want, say that the government is different, because it does not go back on its word.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second answer: when a king decides to build, it will surely get done.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One reason given for רב חסדא's rule is that ordinary people might tear down and then never finish building (the פשיעותא reason from step 15). A king does not give up on his plans, so that worry does not apply. The rule stays the same; the king's case simply has a different outcome.

keyTerms.meaning: Goes back on it / changes its mind

phrases.english: Or if you want, say:
the government is different, because it does not go back on its word;

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: מַלְכוּתָא שָׁאנֵי, דְּלָא הָדְרָא בֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second, separate answer to the same קשיא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Removes the reason behind the rule in this case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every tearing down is risky because the new building may never be finished.
steps.terutzMaskana: A king always carries out his plans, so there is no risk.

steps.title: שמואל: a king will even uproot mountains
steps.stepSummary: שמואל's saying proves that a government carries out what it announces.
steps.simpleTranslation: As שמואל said: if the government says, 'I will uproot mountains,' it uproots mountains and does not back down.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא supports the second answer with a saying of שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל teaches that a government finishes even huge, hard projects once it announces them. That backs up the idea that הורדוס would surely finish rebuilding the בית המקדש.

phrases.english: As Shmuel said:
If the government says, "I will uproot mountains,"
it uproots mountains and does not back down.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings support for the second answer.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that a government does not go back on its plans
steps.whatToRemember: רב חסדא's rule has two exceptions here: a cracked building, and a king who will surely finish building.

steps.title: הורדוס rebels and kills his masters
steps.stepSummary: הורדוס, a slave of בית חשמונאי, hears a heavenly voice, kills his masters, and spares one girl.
steps.simpleTranslation: הורדוס was a slave of בית חשמונאי. He wanted a certain young girl. One day he heard a בת קול say that any slave who rebels now will succeed. He killed all his masters but left that girl alive.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now starts telling the story of הורדוס and בבא בן בוטא. Here it explains how הורדוס rose to power.
steps.deeperAnalysis: הורדוס was not from a royal family; he was a slave. He used the בת קול as a signal to rebel and wiped out the royal family. He kept the girl alive because he wanted her.

phrases.english: Herod was a slave of the house of the Hasmoneans.
He set his eyes on a certain young girl.

phrases.aramaic: יוֹמָא חַד, שְׁמַע הָהוּא גַּבְרָא בַּת קָלָא
phrases.english: One day, that man heard a heavenly voice

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר: כָּל עַבְדָּא דְּמָרֵיד הַשְׁתָּא, מַצְלַח.
phrases.english: that said: Any slave who rebels now will succeed.
He got up and killed all his masters,
and spared that girl.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the background story of the episode mentioned in the קשיא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: הורדוס, a former slave, took the throne by killing the Hasmonean family.

steps.title: The Hasmonean girl's announcement from the roof
steps.stepSummary: The girl declares that anyone claiming Hasmonean descent is a slave, then falls from the roof.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the girl saw he wanted to marry her, she went up to the roof and shouted: 'Anyone who comes and says he is from בית חשמונאי is a slave, because only this girl was left of them, and this girl is falling from the roof to the ground.'
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues: the girl refuses to marry הורדוס and ends her life by falling from the roof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: She did not want הורדוס to claim royal status through her. By announcing that she was the last one, she made sure that anyone later claiming to be a Hasmonean would be exposed as a slave, including הורדוס.

phrases.english: When that girl saw
that he wanted to marry her,
she went up to the roof, raised her voice, and said:

phrases.aramaic: ״כֹּל מַאן דְּאָתֵי וְאָמַר: מִבֵּית חַשְׁמוֹנַאי קָאָתֵינָא
phrases.english: "Anyone who comes and says, 'I come from the house of the Hasmoneans'
is a slave,

phrases.aramaic: דְּלָא אִישְׁתְּיַירָא מִינַּיְיהוּ אֶלָּא הַהִיא יָנוֹקְתָּא,
phrases.english: since no one remained from them except that girl,
phrases.notes: "That girl" is her talking about herself.

phrases.english: and that girl fell from the roof to the ground."
phrases.notes: As she says this, she throws herself down and dies.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי חֲזָת הָהִיא יָנוֹקְתָּא דְּקָא בָּעֵי לְמִינְסְבַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story of the girl הורדוס spared.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The last Hasmonean publicly declared that no true Hasmonean was left after her.

steps.title: הורדוס keeps her body in honey; two versions
steps.stepSummary: הורדוס preserved her body in honey for seven years; there are two opinions about whether he sinned with it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He preserved her in honey for seven years. Some say he had relations with her body; some say he did not.
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues with what הורדוס did with the girl's body. Two opinions are brought.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Honey kept the body from decaying. The two opinions argue about whether הורדוס acted out his desire on the body or not; the next step explains the reason for each view.

phrases.english: He preserved her for seven years in honey.
Some say: he had relations with her body,
and some say: he did not have relations with her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tells what הורדוס did after the girl died.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: הורדוס preserved the body; there is a dispute about whether he sinned with it.

steps.title: Why הורדוס preserved the body, according to each view
steps.stepSummary: Each opinion explains his reason: to satisfy his desire, or so people would think he married a princess.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to those who say he had relations with her, he preserved her to satisfy his desire. According to those who say he did not, he preserved her so people would say he married a king's daughter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reason for preserving the body according to each of the two opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One view: the reason was his own lust. The other view: the reason was political, so people would think he married into the royal family and was a rightful king.

phrases.english: According to those who say he had relations with her,
the reason he preserved her was to satisfy his desire.
And according to those who say he did not have relations with her,
the reason he preserved her was so that people would say:
He married a king's daughter.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמְרִי לַהּ בָּא עָלֶיהָ, הָא דְּטַמְנַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the purpose behind preserving the body for each opinion in the previous step.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Either for lust, or to look like he married royalty.

steps.title: הורדוס kills the רבנן but spares בבא בן בוטא
steps.stepSummary: Because the רבנן taught that a king must be Jewish-born, הורדוס killed them, except בבא בן בוטא, whom he kept for advice.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: Who teaches from the פסוק 'From among your brothers you shall set a king over you'? The רבנן. So he killed all the רבנן, but left בבא בן בוטא alive so he could get advice from him.
steps.whatsHappening: הורדוס goes after the רבנן, because their teaching shows he is not fit to be king. He spares only בבא בן בוטא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן learned from the פסוק that a king must come from a Jewish family, which a former slave is not. To silence that challenge, הורדוס killed them. This brings us back to בבא בן בוטא, who later gives הורדוס the advice about the בית המקדש.

phrases.english: He said: Who teaches from the verse
"From among your brothers you shall set a king over you"?
The Sages.
He got up and killed all the Sages,

phrases.aramaic: שַׁבְקֵיהּ לְבָבָא בֶּן בּוּטָא לְמִשְׁקַל עֵצָה מִנֵּיהּ.
phrases.english: but left Bava ben Buta alive in order to take advice from him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר: מַאן דָּרֵישׁ ״מִקֶּרֶב אַחֶיךָ תָּשִׂים עָלֶיךָ מֶלֶךְ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story and brings בבא בן בוטא into it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: הורדוס killed the רבנן because their teaching made him unfit to be king, sparing only בבא בן בוטא.
steps.whatToRemember: הורדוס was a former slave who took the throne by force. He killed the רבנן who could question his right to rule, but kept בבא בן בוטא as an advisor; this sets up the story of the בית המקדש.
